# Code-review stage assessment

## Scope and evidence

Assess the entire delivered change from `50b661e57973de16a23e801e305160a08b0ae01d` to the review head against REQ-001–018, TASK-001–006, and TC-001–030. The specified base commit exists locally; the earlier coding-stage output names a different base SHA, so the review must use the review task's explicit base and verify its full changed-path set. The current head at assessment is `7a65fdb0abecfdb44bb13c74c2ac2e343b8ee577`; the working tree was clean before this assessment. Approved predecessor outputs are references, not proof that behavior passes.

The supplied image shows a white page with a centered bordered panel, bold "Sign in" heading, labeled stacked email/password inputs, `name@example.com` and masked `********` placeholders, a blue underlined "Forgot password?" link between password and wide dark sign-in button, and a muted "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. Exact dimensions and color codes are not specified. The curated account recovery standard (source reference `knowledge/28e06fb4-ccd1-4117-8f7b-b2a6c9bfaf1f`, v1 chunk 0) requires identical account-existence-independent request responses, five requests per account per hour, single-use links expiring after 30 minutes, sign-out of every active session, and owner notification on every success. The approved test-case design makes the expiry boundary exclusive and calls for a rolling-hour limit.

## Repository and baseline quality gates

The repository is a Python 3.12 `src/`-layout Flask/Jinja application with `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, `uv.lock`, Ruff, and pytest. Routes and application factory are in `src/password_reset_exercise/__init__.py`; synchronized synthetic account, token, session and in-memory notification state is in `state.py`; seven HTML templates and one stylesheet serve pages; seven pytest modules cover the entry and recovery flow. README documents local execution and production limitations. `uv` and `python3.12` are available. Prior coding output reports 40 passing tests and four passing gates but these are not independent review results; the assessment does not execute the review gates ahead of plan approval.

Run the full existing gates during each authorized review/fix round from the repository root: `uv run --python 3.12 python3.12 -m compileall -q src tests` (build), `uv run --python 3.12 python3.12 -m pytest` (all tests), `uv run --python 3.12 ruff check .` and `uv run --python 3.12 ruff format --check .` (all linters). Respect the lockfile and do not install dependencies unless a gate reports they are missing. No database, mail provider, deployment target, or external service is needed; accounts, notifications, and session fixtures are in process. Docker is not required by the observed quality gates.

## Coverage and review risks

Coding-stage evidence maps 24 of 30 cases to automated tests and marks TC-001, TC-002, TC-026, TC-027, TC-028, and TC-029 manual or partially structurally tested. Independently inspect visual hierarchy and accessibility limits, test assertions and fixture fidelity, public response equivalence including at cap, exact rolling-hour and 30-minute boundaries, concurrent single-use updates, account/token binding, session invalidation, private notification visibility, and failure handling. In particular, the sign-in template posts to a GET-only `/sign-in` route while the approved design intentionally leaves sign-in success unspecified; assess whether this is a material broken control rather than inventing an authentication requirement. Inspect all changed paths for workflow/deployment changes and distinguish absence of an observed deployment from proof of full delivery-action history (TC-026). Check that production limitations match actual volatile single-process behavior.

Review output must contain per-requirement coverage for all REQ-001–018, evidence-linked findings with stable `REV-` IDs, and gate status. Use `code-review-findings` severity/blocking rules. The first approved round is read-only for product code; up to two conditional fix/re-review rounds may follow, with `review-r1.json`, `review-r2.json`, `review-r3.json` as applicable and the final version copied to `review.json`. Preserve all earlier finding IDs and statuses. A clean review skips unnecessary conditional rounds. No product edits, deployment, workflow edits, commits, or scope changes are authorized by this assessment.
